app.title: Thaumic Cast
speakers.none: No Sonos speakers have made themselves known
speakers.scan_hint: Ensure you're on the same network as your speakers, then give it a go.
speakers.manual_add_hint: You can also <0>add a speaker manually</0> if discovery isn't cooperating.
server.restart_description: Closes and reopens the app, as one does
server.disconnect_description: Politely but firmly closes all extension connections
settings.autostart_description: Have Thaumic Cast ready and waiting when you arrive
settings.speaker_monitor_description: Works out every few seconds, from each speaker's playback position, how much audio it has in hand. This is what warns you before a speaker runs out, and what drift correction steers by. Turning it off also turns off speaker notices. Takes effect from each speaker's next connection.
settings.speaker_monitor_env_on: THAUMIC_SPEAKER_MONITOR has insisted on this being on, and it outranks the checkbox.
settings.speaker_monitor_env_off: THAUMIC_SPEAKER_MONITOR has insisted on this being off, and it outranks the checkbox.
settings.head_start_description: Audio sent to each speaker as fast as it will take it when it starts playing, so it can ride out Wi-Fi hiccups. It adds the same delay, which video sync allows for. 500 ms suits most homes; raise it if one speaker on a weak Wi-Fi link cuts out. Applies from each speaker's next connection. PCM casts only.
settings.head_start_env: THAUMIC_PCM_CONNECT_BURST_MS has insisted on {{value}} ms, and it outranks the setting.
settings.head_start_env_off: THAUMIC_PCM_CONNECT_BURST_MS has insisted on the head start being off, and it outranks the setting.
settings.drift_description: No two clocks agree exactly, so over a long cast a speaker slowly uses up its head start. Correction stretches or squeezes the audio by a tiny amount, at most 150 parts per million and far too little to hear, to keep each speaker's supply level. PCM casts only.
settings.drift_needs_monitor: Needs Keep an eye on speakers.
settings.drift_env: THAUMIC_DRIFT_COMPENSATION has insisted on {{label}}, and it outranks the setting.
settings.manual_speakers_empty: No speakers have been added by hand
settings.check_for_updates_description: Opens the releases page in your browser
dashboard.speaker_notice_head_start_ran_: Wi-Fi trouble held back {{stall}} ms of audio from {{name}}, more than its {{current}} ms head start covers, so it cut out for a moment. A {{suggested}} ms head start would have covered it.
Wi-Fi trouble held back {{stall}} ms of audio from {{name}}, and with the speaker head start off it cut out for a moment. A {{suggested}} ms head start would have covered it.
dashboard.speaker_notice_head_start_clos: Wi-Fi trouble held back {{stall}} ms of audio from {{name}}, leaving {{left}} ms of its {{current}} ms head start. A {{suggested}} ms head start would leave room to spare.
Wi-Fi trouble held back {{stall}} ms of audio from {{name}}, and with the speaker head start off it nearly cut out. A {{suggested}} ms head start would leave room to spare.
dashboard.speaker_notice_head_start_no_r: Wi-Fi trouble held back {{stall}} ms of audio from {{name}}, more than the longest head start covers. Moving the speaker closer to the router, or connecting it by Ethernet, should help.
dashboard.speaker_notice_where: Change it under Settings > Speakers. It applies from the speaker's next connection, for example when a cast restarts.
dashboard.speaker_notice_where_fixed: THAUMIC_PCM_CONNECT_BURST_MS sets the head start, so change it there.
dashboard.speaker_notice_running_low: {{name}} is down to about {{left}} ms of audio in hand and may cut out.
dashboard.speaker_notice_running_low_dri: It plays slightly faster than the audio arrives.
dashboard.speaker_notice_drift_uncorrect: {{name}} plays slightly faster than the audio arrives and will run low in about {{minutes}} min.
dashboard.speaker_notice_drift_saturated: The clock in {{name}} is further out than drift correction can make up, so it will run low in about {{minutes}} min.
dashboard.speaker_notice_drift_turn_on_d: Turning on clock drift correction in the Thaumic Cast desktop app keeps it topped up.
dashboard.speaker_notice_restart_refills: Stopping and restarting the cast refills it.
network.speakers_not_responding: The speakers have been located but appear to be giving us the silent treatment. A VPN or overzealous firewall is the likely culprit.
network.speakers_unreachable: Your speakers have made themselves scarce. Firewalls and VPNs are the usual suspects.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to Thaumic Cast
onboarding.welcome.subtitle: The server side of the equation
onboarding.welcome.body_windows: This application acts as the bridge between your browser and your Sonos speakers. It lurks quietly in your system tray, ready to channel audio when called upon.
onboarding.welcome.body_macos: This application acts as the bridge between your browser and your Sonos speakers. It lurks quietly in your menu bar, ready to channel audio when called upon.
onboarding.welcome.body_linux: This application acts as the bridge between your browser and your Sonos speakers. It lurks quietly in your system tray, ready to channel audio when called upon.
onboarding.welcome.footnote: Think of it as a very dedicated postal service for sound.
onboarding.firewall.title: A Brief Interruption
onboarding.firewall.prompt_windows: In a moment, Windows will likely ask for permission to allow network access. This is normal and entirely necessary.
onboarding.firewall.prompt_macos: macOS, and any diligent gatekeepers like Little Snitch, may ask about connections to unfamiliar addresses. Some will begin with 224.*. That's multicast, which is a polite way of asking the local network if anyone's in and wants a cup of tea.
onboarding.firewall.prompt_linux: Depending on your firewall configuration, you may need to allow incoming connections on ports 49400-49410.
onboarding.firewall.reason_1: Your browser extension needs to send audio data to this app
onboarding.firewall.reason_2: This app needs to communicate with your Sonos speakers
onboarding.firewall.reason_3: All traffic stays on your local network — nothing leaves your home
onboarding.speakers.title: Discovering Speakers
onboarding.speakers.subtitle: Let's find your Sonos devices
onboarding.speakers.none_found_hint: Speakers can be shy. Check that they're powered on and connected to the same network as this computer.
onboarding.speakers.searching: Searching for speakers on your network...
onboarding.speakers.manual_hint: For networks where discovery has opinions
onboarding.speakers.manual_error_not_son: That doesn't seem to be a Sonos speaker
onboarding.speakers.manual_error_invalid: That doesn't look like an IP address
onboarding.extension.title: The Browser Extension
onboarding.extension.subtitle: The other half of the equation
onboarding.extension.body: You'll need the Thaumic Cast browser extension to capture audio from your tabs. It's the bit that does the actual capturing.
onboarding.extension.skip_hint: You can always install it later from the Chrome Web Store.
onboarding.ready.title: The Ritual is Complete
onboarding.ready.subtitle: Your speakers await instruction
onboarding.ready.intro: You can now stream audio from up to {{maxStreams}} browser tabs simultaneously. The universe has limits, and apparently this is one of them.
onboarding.ready.performance_body: This works best for music. Audio reaches the speakers about a second after it plays, which goes unnoticed with songs but is quite noticeable if you're trying to conduct an orchestra. Turn on video sync to keep films in step.
onboarding.ready.battery_warning: Laptops running on battery power may experience occasional hiccups, as your computer decides that saving energy is more important than your listening pleasure. Browsers can be particularly zealous about this.
onboarding.ready.autostart_description: Have Thaumic Cast ready and waiting when you arrive, like a particularly attentive butler for your audio needs.
